gaps_addressed: UAR process versus embedded execution boundary

candidates.name: Outcome-carried ready uptime
candidates.fit_for_gap: Make retry reset semantics deterministic and measure only post-readiness uptime.

evidence.claim: The existing SupervisionContract already makes attempt outcomes and retry waits injectable; carrying ready uptime completes that seam without a new abstraction.
Each protocol adapter can use a monotonic Instant around only its ready-to-exit interval while tests provide Duration values directly.

risks: Every Retryable construction site must be migrated consistently.
candidates.decision_rationale: Smallest implementation, correct semantic owner, no new dependency, and invalid readiness/uptime combinations are excluded with Option<Duration>.

candidates.name: Injected Clock trait
candidates.fit_for_gap: Substitute monotonic time in policy tests.

evidence.claim: Large Rust systems use clock abstractions where many components independently acquire time.

risks: Adds a trait and production plumbing for one comparison.
Does not by itself move the measurement start from spawn to readiness.
candidates.decision_rationale: More abstraction than the current policy requires and does not solve the semantic boundary alone.

candidates.name: mock_instant 0.6.1

evidence.claim: The crate provides a mock replacement for std::time::Instant.

risks: Adds global/mock clock machinery for one local invariant.
Cannot control subprocess, filesystem, or socket scheduling.
candidates.decision_rationale: The contract can represent elapsed ready time directly with less code and stronger semantics.

candidates.name: Tokio paused time
candidates.fit_for_gap: Control Tokio timers in asynchronous tests.

evidence.claim: Tokio pause controls Tokio's time driver; it does not control std::time::Instant or operating-system process scheduling.

risks: Would preserve the incorrect pre-spawn measurement boundary if used alone.
candidates.decision_rationale: Useful for timer-driven unit tests but not the right seam for this policy or subprocess tests.

candidates.name: Tokio CancellationToken and TaskTracker
candidates.fit_for_gap: Structured in-process lifecycle if UAR later exposes a library service.

evidence.claim: CancellationToken and TaskTracker support cooperative notification and joining of async tasks.
Task abort is cooperative at yield points and cannot abort an already-running spawn_blocking task.

risks: Shared process failure and resource domain remains.
Does not address retry-accounting test design.
candidates.decision_rationale: Relevant to a future supported embedded service API, not to the current defect.

candidates.name: backoff 0.4 / tokio-retry 0.3
candidates.fit_for_gap: Repeat asynchronous operations with exponential backoff.

evidence.claim: backoff supplies exponential retry scheduling for sync and Tokio operations.
tokio-retry wraps futures with extensible retry strategies.

risks: Does not model readiness, terminal errors, endpoint publication, shutdown races, or stable-ready-uptime reset.
Would duplicate rather than replace the domain-specific supervision contract.
candidates.decision_rationale: The generic retry schedule is a small fraction of the existing lifecycle policy; adopting a crate does not remove the domain code under test.

candidates.name: process-wrap 9.1 / generic Rust process supervisors
candidates.fit_for_gap: Wrap child processes with process-group/session/job-object and kill-on-drop controls.

evidence.claim: process-wrap provides platform process groups, sessions, job objects, and kill-on-drop around Command.
The registry contains generic supervisor actors and development-process managers, but none encode UAR's READY/HTTP/EOF protocol.

risks: Adds platform abstraction while leaving the UAR wire and readiness contract untouched.
Could change process-tree semantics outside the requested retry-policy correction.
candidates.decision_rationale: Tokio Command already supplies the process primitives used here; the missing seam is domain outcome data, not process creation.

build_required.need: UAR retained-listener startup and truthful READY/BOUND handshake
build_required.why_no_candidate: The defect is in UAR's own sidecar entry point and server construction; it requires a focused upstream source change, not a third-party library.
